findings.title: hooks/lib/common.sh is installed and validated but never sourced by any hook post-merge
findings.detail: The _log_core refactor (P1-3) did not change common.sh's runtime status. log-tool-calls.sh resolves its own script dir inline (lines 13-17); log-rotate.sh hardcodes LOG_DIR directly; safety hooks need no path resolution. grep confirms zero calls to SCRIPT_DIR_OF, claude_logs_dir, ensure_logs_dir, or extract_jq_field across all production hooks. common.sh is symlinked into ~/.claude/hooks/lib/ by install.sh (line 237 glob), verified by validate.sh (line 65), and documented in README and HOOKS.md — a full installation footprint with zero runtime contribution. This is the same structural problem as M-01 from run 20260426-132457-db430c72; that finding was not assigned a GitHub issue number and was not addressed in any of the 7 in-PR P1 fixes or 5 quick-win commits.
findings.recommendation: Delete common.sh and remove it from the validate.sh symlink check list. Alternatively migrate log-tool-calls.sh's 3-line inline SCRIPT_DIR resolution (lines 13-17) to use SCRIPT_DIR_OF so the library earns its installation footprint. As-is, every future hook author reading lib/ will find common.sh, assume it is canonical, source it, and inherit a macOS/GNU portability shim they never needed.

findings.title: validate.sh hook-presence check still uses the broad .. | objects | .command? walk that install.sh narrowed in the #15 fix
findings.detail: install.sh's idempotency guard was narrowed in commit e9b0610 (the #15 quick-win fix), replacing the broad ".. | objects | .command?" walk with specific hook-event paths (.hooks.PreToolUse, .hooks.PostToolUse, .hooks.SessionEnd). The parallel check in validate.sh line 41 was not updated and still runs "jq -r .. | objects | .command? // empty". The two files now have different false-positive profiles: validate.sh will report a hook as wired if any nested object anywhere in settings.json has a .command field matching the hook name (e.g. inside a comment field, env block, or unrelated config section), while install.sh correctly inspects only actual hook-event paths. A developer debugging why validate.sh reports success while the hook is not wired under PreToolUse will be misled.
findings.recommendation: Update validate.sh line 41 to use the same jq expression as install.sh lines 127-132: walk (.hooks.PreToolUse // [])[]?.hooks[]?.command, (.hooks.PostToolUse // [])[]?.hooks[]?.command, and (.hooks.SessionEnd // [])[]?.hooks[]?.command. Both files must use identical logic for the same semantic check. This is a half-applied fix.

findings.title: Implementation plan document references jsonl-write.py (hyphen) while the shipped file is jsonl_write.py (underscore)
findings.detail: The plan document consistently uses the hyphenated name "hooks/lib/jsonl-write.py" across its Tech Stack section, file structure table, Task 3 heading, and all subprocess.run test invocations. The merged file uses an underscore ("hooks/lib/jsonl_write.py") to match Python module naming conventions. Shipped docs (LOGGING.md, README.md) use the underscore correctly. The plan document is the only source of the stale hyphenated name. Since the plan lives in docs/superpowers/plans/ and is committed to main, a developer doing archaeology to understand how jsonl_write.py was built will encounter subprocess.run calls that reference a path that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Replace all occurrences of "jsonl-write.py" with "jsonl_write.py" in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-26-centralize-claude-config.md. Low priority since plan docs are archeological rather than executable, but the mismatch is a dead reference in a committed file.

residual_risks.description: M-01 from the prior review (common.sh dead) was not given a GitHub issue number and was not addressed by the _log_core refactor or any quick-win commit. It carries forward as M-16. If left unresolved, every future hook author will find SCRIPT_DIR_OF in common.sh, assume it is the canonical way to resolve symlink-aware paths in hooks, source it, and acquire a dependency on a file that has never been exercised in production.

The _log_core refactor correctly eliminated the synchronization risk between the formerly duplicated _PATTERNS copies (M-02/RR-01 from prior review). All three callers now import from a single source. The residual risk is that test-redaction.sh exercises hooks/lib/redact.py as a standalone CLI but does not run the live hook path (log-tool-calls.sh -> log_tool_call.py -> _log_core.redact_value) against a secret-containing fixture and verify the on-disk JSONL is clean. Since _log_core is the shared source this risk is low, but TG-01 from the prior review remains open.

testing_gaps.description: test-redaction.sh exercises hooks/lib/redact.py as a standalone CLI but does not verify that piping a secret-containing fixture through "bash hooks/log-tool-calls.sh pre" produces a JSONL row where the secret is scrubbed. test-hooks.sh lines 84-93 check that the log is created and has correct schema fields but do not assert that secret values are absent from the written output. A test that sends input containing e.g. a GitHub token through the hook and greps the resulting JSONL line for the token would close this gap.

validate.sh's hook-presence check (line 41) is never run by any test in tests/. test-settings-valid.sh checks that settings.json parses and that hook file paths exist on disk, but does not invoke validate.sh. The divergence between validate.sh and install.sh's jq expressions identified in M-17 would be caught if a test ran validate.sh against a synthetic settings.json that wires hooks only under a non-standard path and asserted it returns exit 1.
